elements.element: Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.
elements.evidence: New 9(c)(2) warrants only that "the services will be performed in conformity with this Agreement"; there is no professional and workmanlike / industry-standard performance standard anywhere in Section 9 or Sections 1 or 5.

elements.element: Deliverables or software are warranted to conform to their documentation.
elements.evidence: 9(c)(1): "the Site and any software delivered hereunder will conform in all material respects to the applicable documentation".

elements.element: The software conformance warranty lasts 12 months.
elements.evidence: 9(c)(1): "for a period of twelve (12) months following delivery".
9(c)(2): "for a period of ninety (90) days following performance".

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: 9(c): "HDI shall, at the Company's election, repair or replace the non-conforming software or services".
9(c): "or refund the fees paid for the non-conforming software or services".

elements.element: Vendor warrants compliance with applicable laws.
elements.evidence: No compliance-with-laws warranty is inserted; 9(a) covers only corporate existence, authority, enforceability and non-conflict.

elements.element: Vendor warrants that the Services and Deliverables contain no malicious code.
elements.evidence: No malicious code / virus warranty appears in the inserted 9(c) or elsewhere in Section 9.

elements.element: Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.
elements.evidence: 9(c)(1) gives a twelve (12) month documentation-conformance warranty for the Site and any software delivered, exceeding the 90-day floor.

elements.element: Services are warranted for at least 30 days.
elements.evidence: 9(c)(2) warrants services performance for ninety (90) days following performance, exceeding the 30-day floor.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: 9(c) remedy sentence expressly provides "repair or replace the non-conforming software or services".
9(c) remedy sentence expressly provides "refund the fees paid for the non-conforming software or services".

reasons: Finding status "deviation" is correct: original Section 9 contained only mutual corporate-authority warranties and the Globix acknowledgment, with no conformance warranty, duration or remedy, so the fallback failed on all four material terms.

The fallback checklist is complete in operative language: documentation conformance for the Site and software (12 months), a 90-day services warranty, and an express repair/replace-or-refund remedy in the same subsection.

Preferred level is not reached: the professional and workmanlike performance standard, the compliance-with-applicable-laws warranty and the no-malicious-code warranty are all absent; to move to preferred the drafter would need to add "performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards" and separate compliance-with-laws and no-malicious-code warranties.

Minimal: the edit is a single concise insertion (new 9(c)), adds no survival tail, no notice or claim procedure, no at-own-expense or damages language, and leaves 9(a) and 9(b) untouched. Note only that the remedy election is placed with the Company rather than the Vendor (model language uses "at Vendor's option") — a customer-favourable mechanic within the required remedy element, not an out-of-checklist addition.

Preserves intent: no "AS IS" clause or implied-warranty disclaimer exists in the cited text, so no carve-out was needed and none was added; the retained mutual warranties and the Globix carve-out are not contradicted, and "the Site", "software delivered hereunder" and "the services" track the existing Section 1/5 obligations without creating undefined terms or dangling cross-references.
Party direction is correct: the warranty runs from HDI (the developing/hosting vendor) to the Company (our client).
